newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Natural Gas sees record gas sales in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Natural Gas sees record gas sales in 96/97.

text.p: Natural Gas Corp on Wednesday said it expected to achieve record gas sales in 1996/97 in a growing market.
Chief Executive Richard Bentley told shareholders at the annual meeting that NGC gas sales could exceed 50 petajoules for the first time in 1996/97.
New loads during the year could add up to 10 petajoules to the company's sales, an increase of 23 percent on the 42.8 petajoules of gas sold in the year to June 30, 1996.

The projection included an agreement, reached in the new competitive gas trading environment, for Natural Gas Corporation to deliver five petajoules of gas to the Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ) over the next 12 months for thermal power generation.
Bentley said first quarter gas sales for 1996/97 had begun well with volumes up 2.5 percent on the corresponding three months last year.

NGC looked forward to significant new gas loads with the commencement of supplies to the new Southdown power station in Auckland, and to the recently commissioned cogeneration plant at Bay Milks Edgecumbe factory.
Bentley said he was hopeful that the joint natural Gas Corporation - Bay of Plenty 25MW cogeneration plant proposed for construction at the Kapuni gas treatment plant would be on stream in late 1997.

Bentley said that while he expected competition in wholesale gas markets to increase significantly during the coming year, the market for gas was expanding and he was confident that NGC would continue to achieve improved operating results through sales growth and cost efficiencies.
